'''''The Last Duel''''' is a 2021 [[epic film|epic]] [[historical drama]] film<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rogerebert.com/reviews/the-last-duel-movie-review-2021|title=The Last Duel movie review & film summary (2021)|website=[[RogerEbert.com]]|access-date=12 October 2021|quote=Nevertheless, while “The Last Duel” may be a partial model of mindfulness, it still obeys the requirements of the period action drama.|archive-date=October 12, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211012140925/https://www.rogerebert.com/reviews/the-last-duel-movie-review-2021|url-status=live}}</ref> directed by [[Ridley Scott]] from a screenplay by [[Nicole Holofcener]], [[Ben Affleck]], and [[Matt Damon]], based on the 2004 book ''[[The Last Duel: A True Story of Crime, Scandal, and Trial by Combat in Medieval France]]'' by [[Eric Jager]]. Set in [[France in the Middle Ages|14th century France]], the film stars Damon as [[Jean de Carrouges]], a knight who challenges his former friend, squire [[Jacques le Gris]] ([[Adam Driver]]), to a [[Trial by combat|judicial duel]] after Jean's wife, [[Marguerite de Carrouges|Marguerite]] ([[Jodie Comer]]), accuses Jacques of raping her. The events leading up to the duel are divided into three distinct chapters, reflecting the contradictory perspectives of the three main characters. Affleck also stars in a supporting role as Count [[Peter II, Count of Alençon|Pierre d'Alençon]].

An adaptation of Jager's book was first announced in 2015, though it was not officially greenlit until July 2019. Affleck and Damon were confirmed as stars and co-writers that month, with Comer and Driver joining the cast later that year. Filming took place in France and Ireland from February to October 2020, with a hiatus of several months due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].

''The Last Duel'' premiered at the [[78th Venice International Film Festival]] on September 10, 2021, and was theatrically released in the United States on October 15, 2021, by [[20th Century Studios]]. The film received generally positive reviews from critics, and was selected by the [[National Board of Review]] as one of the [[National Board of Review Awards 2021|top ten films of 2021]]. Although the film was a [[box-office bomb]], it later found financial success in post-theatrical markets.<ref>{{cite web |last=Helm |first=Douglas |date=January 23, 2022 |title=A Highly-Rated Matt Damon Flop is a Hit on Streaming |url=https://www.giantfreakinrobot.com/ent/matt-damon-streaming-last-duel.html |website=Giant Freakin Robot}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Campbell |first=Scott |date=December 31, 2021 |title='The Last Duel' gets reappraised after people actually watch it |url=https://wegotthiscovered.com/movies/the-last-duel-gets-reappraised-after-people-actually-watch-it/ |website=WGTC}}</ref>

==Plot==
''While the plot of the film is portrayed in three separate chapters, each telling the same story from the perspective of the three main characters, the following description summarizes all three presentations into a single narrative:''

After serving in the [[Caroline War]], French squire [[Jean de Carrouges]] and his comrade [[Jacques le Gris]] swear allegiance to Count [[Peter II, Count of Alençon|Pierre d'Alençon]], who has been named Jean's overlord by [[Charles VI of France|King Charles VI]]. To improve his finances, Jean marries [[Marguerite de Thibouville]] on the promise of a large [[dowry]] from her father Robert that includes the rights to many valuable estates. Pierre, however, seizes the prized estate of [[Aunou-le-Faucon]] to settle Robert's back taxes and gifts it to Jacques, who has become one of Pierre's favorites. Jean appeals to King Charles, but the king upholds Pierre's decision, and the count exacts revenge by depriving Jean of a prominent captaincy previously held by his late father and gifting it to Jacques, making him superior to Jean in rank.

Jean's marriage becomes strained due to the couple's failure to conceive. He and Jacques reconcile at a celebration, where Jacques becomes smitten with Marguerite after she befriends him in an attempt to win favor. Jacques misinterprets this as a reciprocation of his affections, coming to believe she actually does not love Jean.

Following his participation in a failed military campaign in [[Kingdom of Scotland|Scotland]] that sees him knighted but still bankrupt, Jean sets off for Paris to collect his promised rewards. Marguerite demonstrates a talent for managing the estate in his absence; while collecting taxes from her peasants, she also learns Jean regularly defers the poorest from their obligation. One day, when Marguerite is left alone at the chateau, Jacques visits and tricks his way in, haughtily proclaiming his love. Marguerite rejects his advances and attempts to flee, but he chases her to her room and rapes her before ordering her not to tell her husband. Upon Jean's return, Marguerite tells him of the assault; after questioning whether she is telling the truth, Jean becomes convinced that Jacques raped Marguerite to insult him specifically. Jean insists that Marguerite immediately have sex with him so that Jacques will not be "the last man that knew her."

Pierre informs Jacques that Jean is accusing him of raping Marguerite, which he denies. Despite the count's attempt to exert his authority, Jean appeals his case directly to King Charles and requests a duel to the death. Jacques accepts, having decided not to seek a favorable forum of a Catholic [[ecclesiastical court]]. Marguerite's friends abandon her, believing her to be lying to cover up an affair, while Jean's mother, who was also raped as a youth but never revealed the truth, insists Marguerite drop her accusations. At Jacques' trial six months later, a now-pregnant Marguerite remains resolute that she is telling the truth, while the court implies that Jacques is the father of her child. Charles grants Jean's request for a duel to determine the case. Marguerite is also informed that she will be burned alive for [[perjury]] if her husband loses and confronts Jean for not telling her about this. She gives birth to her son not long before the duel takes place.

[[File:Duel entre Jacques Le Gris et Jean de Carrouges.png|thumb|A historic depiction of the duel (1480)]]

The duel begins with Jean and Jacques [[jousting]] until both men lose their mounts and fight hand-to-hand. Following a lengthy struggle, Jean is stabbed in the thigh but eventually manages to pin down Jacques. He demands that Jacques confess or face damnation, but Jacques claims his innocence. Jean then kills him. Jean basks in the glory of his victory while Marguerite follows quietly behind. Meanwhile, Jacques' body is stripped and hung upside down publicly whilst Pierre looks on.

An epilogue reveals Jean died fighting in the [[Battle of Nicopolis|Crusades]] while Marguerite continued managing his estate, living in peace for the remainder of her life but never remarrying.

=== Music ===
{{Main|The Last Duel (soundtrack)}}
Harry Gregson-Williams composed the film score, in his third collaboration with Scott as a composer after ''[[Kingdom of Heaven (film)|Kingdom of Heaven]]'' (2005) and ''[[The Martian (film)|The Martian]]'' (2015).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Tangcay |first=Jazz |date=2021-10-15 |title=How Ridley Scott's 'The Last Duel' Crafted a Medieval World Through Costumes, Music and Lighting |url=https://variety.com/2021/artisans/news/costumes-last-duel-score-cinematography-1235089533/ ==Release==
''The Last Duel'' was originally scheduled to begin a limited theatrical release on December 25, 2020, before its wide release on January 8, 2021.<ref name="DisneyFox schedule" /> As a result of the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], the release date was pushed back a year to October 15, 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |last=D'Alessandro |first=Anthony |date=July 23, 2020 |title='Mulan' Off The Calendar; Disney Also Delays 'Avatar' & 'Star Wars' Movies By One Year As Studio Adjusts To Pandemic |url=https://deadline.com/2020/07/mulan-avatar-star-wars-release-date-changes-disney-coroanvirus-1202993719/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200724215648/https://deadline.com/2020/07/mulan-avatar-star-wars-release-date-changes-disney-coroanvirus-1202993719/ |archive-date=July 24, 2020 |access-date=July 23, 2020 |website=Deadline Hollywood}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Rubin |first=Rebecca |date=July 23, 2020 |title='Star Wars' Films, 'Avatar' Sequels Pushed Back a Year in Disney Release Calendar Shakeup |work=Variety |url=https://variety.com/2020/film/box-office/star-wars-films-avatar-sequels-pushed-back-a-year-in-disney-release-calendar-shakeup-1234715104/ |url-status=live |access-date=July 23, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200723212010/https://variety.com/2020/film/box-office/star-wars-films-avatar-sequels-pushed-back-a-year-in-disney-release-calendar-shakeup-1234715104/ |archive-date=July 23, 2020}}</ref> It had its world premiere at the [[78th Venice International Film Festival]] on September 10, 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Vivarelli |first=Nick |date=July 26, 2021 |title=Venice Film Festival Full Lineup Unveiled – Live Updates |url=https://variety.com/2021/film/news/venice-film-festival-2021-lineup-1235027083/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210802151959/https://variety.com/2021/film/news/venice-film-festival-2021-lineup-1235027083/ |archive-date=August 2, 2021 |access-date=July 26, 2021 |website=Variety}}</ref> The film played exclusively in theaters for 45 days before it headed to digital platforms.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Vary |first1=Adam B. |last2=Saperstein |first2=Pat |date=September 10, 2021 |title=Disney Releasing 'Eternals,' 'Encanto' Exclusively in Theaters |url=https://variety.com/2021/film/news/eternals-encanto-west-side-story-last-duel-theaters-disney-1235061504/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210910215817/https://variety.com/2021/film/news/eternals-encanto-west-side-story-last-duel-theaters-disney-1235061504/ |archive-date=September 10, 2021 |access-date=September 10, 2021 |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]}}</ref>

===Home media===
The film was released on digital platforms and premium video-on-demand on November 30, 2021, and on [[Blu-ray]], DVD and Ultra HD Blu-ray on December 14, 2021, by [[Walt Disney Studios Home Entertainment]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Remley |first=Hilary |date=November 8, 2021 |title=''The Last Duel'' Gets 4K and Blu-ray Release Date in Time for Christmas |url=https://collider.com/the-last-duel-4k-blu-ray-release-date-details/ |access-date=November 25, 2021 |website=Collider}}</ref>

''The Last Duel'' became available for streaming on [[HBO Max]] on January 14, 2022. According to the streaming aggregator [[JustWatch]], ''The Last Duel'' was the 2nd most watched film across all platforms in the United States, during the week ending January 16, 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gruenwedel |first=Erik |date=2022-01-18 |title=JustWatch: Apple's 'The Tragedy of Macbeth' Scores Streaming Movie Win |url=https://www.mediaplaynews.com/justwatch-apples-the-tragedy-of-macbeth-scores-streaming-movie-win/ |access-date=2022-10-31 |website=Media Play News |language=en-US |archive-date=February 23, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220223050651/https://www.mediaplaynews.com/justwatch-apples-the-tragedy-of-macbeth-scores-streaming-movie-win/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Reception==
===Box office===
''The Last Duel'' grossed $10.9&nbsp;million in the United States and Canada and $19.7&nbsp;million in other territories, for a worldwide total of $30.6{{nbsp}}million.<ref name="BOM" /><ref name="NUM" />

In the United States and Canada, ''The Last Duel'' was initially projected to gross around $10&nbsp;million from 3,065 theaters in its opening weekend.<ref name="VarietyProj">{{Cite web |last=Rubin |first=Rebecca |date=October 13, 2021 |title=Box Office: 'Halloween Kills' Hunting Down $40 Million Debut as 'The Last Duel' Eyes Scary Start |url=https://variety.com/2021/film/box-office/box-office-halloween-kills-opening-weekend-estimate-jamie-lee-curtis-1235087961/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211016154557/https://variety.com/2021/film/box-office/box-office-halloween-kills-opening-weekend-estimate-jamie-lee-curtis-1235087961/amp/ |archive-date=October 16, 2021 |access-date=October 13, 2021 |website=Variety |language=en-US}}</ref> After making $1.8&nbsp;million on its first day, including $350,000 from Thursday night previews, estimates were lowered to $5&nbsp;million. It ended up debuting to $4.8&nbsp;million, finishing fifth at the box office and marking the worst opening of Scott's career.<ref name="Variety-BO">{{Cite web |last=Lang |first=Brent |date=October 17, 2021 |title=Box Office: 'Halloween Kills' Scores Bloody Great $50.4 Million Debut, 'The Last Duel' Bombs |url=https://variety.com/2021/film/news/box-office-halloween-kills-debut-matt-damon-ben-affleck-last-duel-bombs-1235091240/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211017152015/https://variety.com/2021/film/news/box-office-halloween-kills-debut-matt-damon-ben-affleck-last-duel-bombs-1235091240/ |archive-date=October 17, 2021 |access-date=October 17, 2021 |website=Variety |language=en-US}}</ref> ''[[Deadline Hollywood]]'' attributed the underperformance to the two-and-a-half-hour runtime limiting the number of showings, the subject matter being hard to market, the 45+ age demo not fully returning to theaters yet, and competition from ''[[Halloween Kills]]'' and ''[[No Time to Die]]''.<ref name="opening">{{Cite web |last=D'Alessandro |first=Anthony |date=October 17, 2021 |title='Halloween Kills' Grabs Best Horror & R-Rated Opening Records During Pandemic With $50.4M, Even With Peacock Day & Date |url=https://deadline.com/2021/10/halloween-kills-the-last-duel-weekend-box-office-1234856404/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211019081020/https://deadline.com/2021/10/halloween-kills-the-last-duel-weekend-box-office-1234856404/ |archive-date=October 19, 2021 |access-date=October 16, 2021 |website=Deadline Hollywood |language=en-US}}</ref> Several publications labeled the film a [[box-office bomb]], and noted that 20th Century would likely lose millions on it.<ref name=Variety-BO/><ref>{{Cite news |last=Poisuo |first=Pauli |date=October 18, 2021 |title=Why Ridley Scott's The Last Duel Bombed at the Box Office |language=en-US |work=Looper |url=https://www.looper.com/635516/why-ridley-scotts-the-last-duel-bombed-at-the-box-office/ |url-status=live |access-date=October 20, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211020142616/https://www.looper.com/635516/why-ridley-scotts-the-last-duel-bombed-at-the-box-office/?utm_campaign=clip |archive-date=October 20, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=McClintock |first=Pamela |date=October 18, 2021 |title='The Last Duel' Box Office Debacle: Hollywood's Battle for Older Moviegoers |language=en-US |work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/the-last-duel-box-office-debacle-1235032811/ |url-status=live |access-date=October 20, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211020001050/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/the-last-duel-box-office-debacle-1235032811/ |archive-date=October 20, 2021}}</ref> It fell 55% in its second weekend to $2.1&nbsp;million, falling to seventh.<ref>{{Cite web |last=D'Alessandro |first=Anthony |date=October 24, 2021 |title='Dune' Domestic Opening Is Best For Warner Bros HBO Max Day/Date Title & Denis Villeneuve |url=https://deadline.com/2021/10/dune-weekend-box-office-1234860683/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211024022240/https://deadline.com/2021/10/dune-weekend-box-office-1234860683/ |archive-date=October 24, 2021 |access-date=October 24, 2021 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]}}</ref> The third weekend saw a drop of 78% to $558,000, for a domestic gross of around $10 million.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mendelson |first=Scott |date=October 31, 2021 |title=Box Office: New Releases Bomb As 'Venom 2' Nears $400 Million |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/scottmendelson/2021/10/31/weekend-box-office-venom-halloween-my-hero-academia-last-night-in-soho-ghostbusters/?sh=75aa9dfe344a |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211104213112/https://gum.criteo.com/syncframe?origin=publishertag&topUrl=www.forbes.com |archive-date=November 4, 2021 |access-date=November 1, 2021 |website=[[Forbes]]}}</ref>

During an interview on the podcast ''[[WTF with Marc Maron]]'' in November 2021, Scott blamed the film's box-office failure on [[millennials]], saying: "I think what it boils down to — what we've got today [are] the audiences who were brought up on these fucking cell phones. The millennian do not ever want to be taught anything unless you are told it on the cell phone".<ref>{{Cite news |last=Hailu |first=Selome |date=November 22, 2021 |title=Ridley Scott Blames Millennials for 'The Last Duel' Box Office Failure |work=Variety |url=https://variety.com/2021/film/news/ridley-scott-blames-millennials-last-duel-flop-1235117654/ |url-status=live |access-date=November 22, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211122233637/https://variety.com/2021/film/news/ridley-scott-blames-millennials-last-duel-flop-1235117654/ |archive-date=November 22, 2021}}</ref> Ben Affleck, who co-wrote the film with co-lead Matt Damon and Nicole Holofcener, was more measured in his assessment of the film's financial failure:<blockquote>I've had bad movies that didn't work and I didn't blink. I know why people didn't go–because they weren't good. But I liked what we did. I like what we had to say. I'm really proud of it. So I was really confused. And then to see that it did well on streaming, I thought, "Well, there you go. That's where the audience is."<ref>{{cite magazine | url=https://ew.com/movies/ben-affleck-cover-story-tender-bar-matt-damon/ | title=Ben Affleck, at the top of his game | magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]] | access-date=January 9, 2023 | archive-date=August 11, 2022 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220811010659/https://ew.com/movies/ben-affleck-cover-story-tender-bar-matt-damon/ | url-status=live }}</ref></blockquote>

===Critical response===
{{Rotten Tomatoes prose|<!--score-->85|<!--rating -->7.3|<!--number of reviews-->287}} The website's critics consensus reads: "''The Last Duel''{{'}}s critique of systemic misogyny isn't as effective as it might have been, but it remains a well-acted and thought-provoking drama infused with epic grandeur."<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/the_last_duel_2021|title=The Last Duel (2021)|website=[[Rotten Tomatoes]]|publisher=[[Fandango Media|Fandango]]|access-date={{RT data|access date}}|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211026161539/https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/the_last_duel_2021|archive-date=October 26, 2021|url-status=live}}{{RT data|edit}}</ref> On [[Metacritic]], the film has a weighted average score of 67 out of 100 based on 50 critics, indicating "generally favorable" reviews.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Last Duel Reviews |url=https://www.metacritic.com/movie/the-last-duel |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211025061027/https://www.metacritic.com/movie/the-last-duel |archive-date=October 25, 2021 |access-date=October 24, 2021 |website=[[Metacritic]]}}</ref> Audiences polled by [[CinemaScore]] gave the film an average grade of "B+" on an A+ to F scale, while those at [[PostTrak]] gave it a 72% positive score.<ref name="opening" />

[[Owen Gleiberman]] of ''[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]'' considered the film "intriguing but overcooked", writing: "Despite a brief action interlude here or there, ''The Last Duel'' turns out to be a lavishly convoluted and, at times, rather interesting medieval soap opera."<ref>{{Cite news |last=Gleiberman |first=Owen |title='The Last Duel' Review: Matt Damon and Adam Driver in Ridley Scott's Intriguing but Overcooked Medieval Soap Opera |work=Variety |url=https://variety.com/2021/film/reviews/the-last-duel-review-matt-damon-adam-driver-ben-affleck-jodie-comer-ridley-scott-1235059966/ |url-status=live |access-date=October 13, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211019052717/https://variety.com/2021/film/reviews/the-last-duel-review-matt-damon-adam-driver-ben-affleck-jodie-comer-ridley-scott-1235059966/amp/ |archive-date=October 19, 2021}}</ref> Reviewing the film for ''[[TheWrap]]'', Asher Luberto praised the performances and cinematography while criticizing the screenplay, writing: "Adapting Eric Jager's 2004 non-fiction book with screenwriters Matt Damon, Ben Affleck and Nicole Holofcener, Scott spins a medieval yarn that is by turns gruesome, grotesque, gorgeous and inconsistent."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Luberto |first=Asher |date=September 10, 2021 |title='The Last Duel' Film Review: Matt Damon's Medieval Hero Outshines Ridley Scott's Muddled Mystery |url=https://www.thewrap.com/the-last-duel-film-review-ridley-scott-matt-damon-adam-driver/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211015023447/https://www.thewrap.com/the-last-duel-film-review-ridley-scott-matt-damon-adam-driver/ |archive-date=October 15, 2021 |access-date=October 14, 2021 |website=[[TheWrap]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

Ben Croll of ''[[IndieWire]]'', who gave the film a "B+" grade, praised it as "something all too rare on the current Hollywood field of battle: an intelligent and genuinely daring big budget melee that is — above all else — the product of recognizable artistic collaboration."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Croll |first=Ben |date=September 10, 2021 |title='The Last Duel' Review: Forget the Bad Hair, Ridley Scott's Epic Is Heir to a Tradition of Movies for Adults |url=https://www.indiewire.com/2021/09/the-last-duel-review-1234663613/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211011011500/https://www.indiewire.com/2021/09/the-last-duel-review-1234663613/ |archive-date=October 11, 2021 |access-date=October 13, 2021 |website=[[IndieWire]] |language=en-US}}</ref> [[Kyle Smith (critic)|Kyle Smith]] of ''[[National Review]]'' wrote that the film was "absolutely soaked in fascinating strangeness", adding: "It works because it doesn’t try to retrofit the facts of the past to fit the assumptions of the present."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Kyle |author-link=Kyle Smith (critic) |date=October 13, 2021 |title=Medieval Madness |url=https://www.nationalreview.com/2021/10/movie-review-the-last-duel-medieval-madness/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211104213028/https://www.nationalreview.com/2021/10/movie-review-the-last-duel-medieval-madness/ |archive-date=November 4, 2021 |access-date=October 18, 2021 |website=National Review |language=en-US}}</ref>

Linda Marric of ''[[The Jewish Chronicle]]'' gave the film a score of five out of five stars, describing it as "a true return to form for Scott and a brilliant testament to Affleck and Damon's unparalleled screenwriting expertise."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Marric |first=Linda |date=October 15, 2021 |title=Film review: The Last Duel |url=https://www.thejc.com/life/film-review-the-last-duel-gj95xr6n |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211018015832/https://www.thejc.com/culture/film/film-review-the-last-duel-1.521602 |archive-date=October 18, 2021 |access-date=October 18, 2021 |website=The Jewish Chronicle}}</ref> Deborah Ross of ''[[The Spectator]]'' described the film as "bleak, brutal and bloody with little respite – aside from Affleck's Count Pierre, who is nicely bitchy."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ross |first=Deborah |title=Hang in there for the gripping final half an hour: The Last Duel reviewed |url=https://www.spectator.co.uk/article/hang-in-there-for-the-gripping-final-half-an-hour-the-last-duel-reviewed |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211019114820/https://www.spectator.co.uk/article/hang-in-there-for-the-gripping-final-half-an-hour-the-last-duel-reviewed |archive-date=October 19, 2021 |access-date=October 20, 2021 |website=The Spectator |date=October 14, 2021 |language=en}}</ref> [[Kevin Maher (writer)|Kevin Maher]] of ''[[The Times]]'' gave the film a score of four out of five, describing it as "a medieval epic that is perhaps [Scott's] most modern movie yet".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Maher |first=Kevin |date=October 15, 2021 |title=The Last Duel review – a thoroughly modern medieval epic |url=https://www.thetimes.com/culture/film/article/the-last-duel-review-bloodthirsty-tale-of-chivalry-cuts-three-ways-8mc259s2s |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211031235545/https://www.thetimes.co.uk/article/the-last-duel-review-bloodthirsty-tale-of-chivalry-cuts-three-ways-8mc259s2s |archive-date=October 31, 2021 |access-date=October 31, 2021 |website=[[The Times]]}}</ref>

Reviewers from [[NPR]]'s ''[[Fresh Air]]'',<ref>{{Cite news |last=Chang |first=Justin |date=October 14, 2021 |title='The Last Duel' is a 'Rashomon'-style #MeToo story – and a messy medieval epic |language=en |work=Fresh Air |publisher=National Public Radio |url=https://www.npr.org/2021/10/15/1045633461/the-last-duel-movie-review}}</ref> ''[[The Atlantic]]'',<ref>{{Cite news |last=Sims |first=David |date=October 13, 2021 |title=Ridley Scott's New Film Plays a Masterly Trick |language=en |work=The Atlantic |url=https://www.theatlantic.com/culture/archive/2021/10/in-the-last-duel-men-are-unreliable-narrators/620377/ |access-date=November 23, 2021}}</ref> ''[[The A.V. Club]]'',<ref>{{Cite news |last=Dowd |first=A.A. |date=October 12, 2021 |title=Ridley Scott offers his own Rashomon with star-studded The Last Duel |language=en-us |work=The A.V. Club |url=https://www.avclub.com/ridley-scott-offers-his-own-rashomon-with-the-star-stud-1847850421 |access-date=November 23, 2021}}</ref> and [[CNN]]<ref name="cnn 2021-10-14">{{Cite web |last=Lowry |first=Brian |date=October 14, 2021 |title='The Last Duel' doesn't disappoint, but the lengthy buildup to it does |url=https://www.cnn.com/2021/10/14/entertainment/the-last-duel-review/index.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211016121224/https://www.cnn.com/2021/10/14/entertainment/the-last-duel-review/index.html |archive-date=October 16, 2021 |access-date=October 18, 2021 |website=CNN}}</ref> all compared ''The Last Duel'' to [[Akira Kurosawa]]'s film ''[[Rashomon]]'' (1950). [[Mark Kermode]] of ''[[The Observer]]'' gave the film a score of three out of five stars, saying that it "plays like an armour-clad reimagining of ''Rashomon'' crossed with a [[Me Too movement|#MeToo]]-inflected remake of ''[[Straw Dogs (1971 film)|Straw Dogs]]''." He added that the film "has a tendency to mirror its central battle's attempts to address complex issues with the blunt tool of rabble-rousing spectacle."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kermode |first=Mark |date=October 17, 2021 |title=The Last Duel review – swordplay without subtlety |url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/2021/oct/17/the-last-duel-review-ridley-scott-jodie-comer-matt-damon-adam-driver |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211018134321/https://www.theguardian.com/film/2021/oct/17/the-last-duel-review-ridley-scott-jodie-comer-matt-damon-adam-driver |archive-date=October 18, 2021 |access-date=October 18, 2021 |website=The Guardian |language=en}}</ref>

Charlotte O'Sullivan of the ''[[Evening Standard]]'' gave the film three out of five stars, describing it as "a handsome, well-researched drama that's by turns earnest, amusing and unintentionally funny."<ref>{{Cite web |last=O'Sullivan |first=Charlotte |date=October 15, 2021 |title=The Last Duel takes aim at misogyny but never lands a killer blow |url=https://www.standard.co.uk/culture/film/the-last-duel-review-move-jodie-comer-ben-affleck-matt-damon-ridley-scott-b960282.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211020112755/https://www.standard.co.uk/culture/film/the-last-duel-review-move-jodie-comer-ben-affleck-matt-damon-ridley-scott-b960282.html |archive-date=October 20, 2021 |access-date=October 20, 2021 |website=Evening Standard |language=en}}</ref> [[Joe Morgenstern]] of ''[[The Wall Street Journal]]'' praised the film's production values, performances and primary theme, but wrote: "the narrative is cluttered with court intrigue against a background of repetitive battles, and the storytelling structure is exhausting."<ref>{{Cite news |last=Morgenstern |first=Joe |date=October 13, 2021 |title='Last Duel': Big Talents, Blunt Swords |language=en-US |work=Wall Street Journal |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/last-duel-big-talents-blunt-swords-jodie-comer-matt-damon-ben-affleck-adam-driver-ridley-scott-eric-jager-alex-lawther-medieval-knights-france-killing-eve-good-will-hunting-the-martian-free-guy-11634140132 |url-status=live |access-date=October 18, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211018113312/https://www.wsj.com/articles/last-duel-big-talents-blunt-swords-jodie-comer-matt-damon-ben-affleck-adam-driver-ridley-scott-eric-jager-alex-lawther-medieval-knights-france-killing-eve-good-will-hunting-the-martian-free-guy-11634140132 |archive-date=October 18, 2021 |issn=0099-9660}}</ref> Brian Lowry of [[CNN]] wrote that the film "is muddy, bloody and grim but too drawn out in filtering 14th-century feudal norms through a modern prism."<ref name="cnn 2021-10-14"/> David Fear of ''[[Rolling Stone]]'' said that the film "ends up perching so close to parody at times that you'd swear the full title was ''[[Monty Python]]'s The Last Duel''."<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Fear |first=David |date=October 13, 2021 |title='The Last Duel': Damon and Affleck Reunite for a Medieval #MeToo-Drama Fail |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/movies/movie-reviews/last-duel-movie-review-matt-damon-adam-driver-1240548/ |url-status=live |magazine=Rolling Stone |language=en-US
